title: ‘Them and us’: Lessons learnt in an educator – therapist collaboration
journal: African Journal of Teacher Education and Development
abstract: Background: Children in South African low quintile schools face multiple barriers to learning, with handwriting difficulties being a key concern. Access to on-site occupational therapy (OT) is limited because of human resource constraints. In response, final-year OT students from the University of Cape Town collaborated with Grade R educators at a low quintile school, training them to implement an educator-led, classroom-based fine motor programme. This approach was guided by evidence supporting collaborative, contextually relevant interventions. Aim: The study aimed to describe educators’ experiences of the training and explore factors influencing the implementation of the fine motor programme. Setting: Low quintile primary school in the Western Cape, Cape Town. Methods: A qualitative, descriptive design was used. Three Grade R educators were purposively selected and trained. Two focus group discussions were conducted to gather their perspectives on the training and implementation process. Data were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim and analysed inductively to identify themes and categories. Results: The central theme, ‘them and us’, captured the divide between stakeholders. A lack of communication, exclusion, unclear role expectations and resistance to change emerged as key challenges. These issues limited collaboration and undermined opportunities for shared learning and mutual support. Conclusion: Collaborative school-based OT requires deliberate investment in relationship-building and role clarification. Contribution: Without these, inclusive and effective implementation of interventions remains unlikely, and learner development may be compromised.

title: Why Did the Kyivan Clergy Need Metropolitans Canonized in Muscovy? Toward a History of Church Reforms in the First Half of the Seventeenth Century
abstract: Abstract In the first half of the seventeenth century, church reforms intensified in the Kyivan Orthodox Metropolitanate, prompted by confrontation with rival confessions. The reforms also included the formation and promotion of the Metropolitanate’s own confessional identity, emphasizing its own importance and spiritual power through the cults of the saints. To emphasize the fullness of its own Church, it was necessary, among other things, to demonstrate that the Kyivan Metropolitanate, like other Orthodox Churches, had its own canonized first-throned hierarchs. This article analyses how Kyivan intellectuals incorporated the names of Metropolitans canonized in Muscovy into the pantheon of their “own” saints during the reforms, and how they later tried to find a replacement for these metropolitans.

title: When platforms integrate generative AI: the dynamics of professional contribution in artist communities
abstract: Purpose Generative AI (GAI) is transforming user-generated content (UGC) communities, yet its impact on professional creators remains underexplored. This study examines how the platform-level integration of a GAI illustration tool into an online artist community influences designers' original content contributions and how these effects vary by designer characteristics. Design/methodology/approach We use 12 months of panel data on 43,587 active designers from a leading online creative platform. Leveraging the platform's introduction of a free GAI illustration tool in October 2022 as a natural experiment, we employ a difference-in-differences design to estimate its effect on designers' original work postings. Findings The results indicate that integrating the GAI tool increases original content contributions by 25%. This effect is driven by multiple mechanisms, including competitive pressure, learning-oriented engagement, and copyright concerns. In particular, competitive pressure induces strategic effort reallocation, leading designers to reduce contributions within their primary domains and shift effort toward less-affected creative areas. Moderation analyses further show that this reallocation effect is stronger among newer and lower-reputation designers. Originality/value Amid growing interest in the impact of GAI, this study centers on the creative domain, shifting the focus from GAI's influence on creative processes to its effects on professional content contributions in online communities. It identifies key mechanisms – competitive pressure, learning-oriented engagement, and copyright concerns – arising from platform-level GAI integration. The findings provide theoretical and practical insights for managing creative platforms in the era of GAI integration.

title: Volunteer involvement at the heart of dementia care: case studies in practice from Dementia Adventure
journal: Quality in Ageing and Older Adults
abstract: Purpose This practice-based paper aims to explore the contribution of volunteers within Dementia Adventure, a UK charity delivering supported breaks, days out and outdoor-based activities for people living with dementia and their carers. It also examines how volunteering contributes to personal and professional development. Design/methodology/approach A practice-based case study approach was used to explore volunteer experiences within the organisational context. Three cases were purposively selected from 125 active volunteers to reflect different volunteer pathways, roles and levels of engagement. The case accounts drew on organisational records, volunteer feedback and reflections and one semi-structured Zoom interview. These materials were reviewed inductively to identify recurring practice themes. The cases are presented as illustrative examples within a structured volunteer programme. Findings Volunteers support people living with dementia and their carers in accessing meaningful outdoor experiences. Their involvement supports personal development, professional skills and a sense of purpose, while also strengthening service delivery, relational support and organisational advocacy. The cases also illustrate how some volunteers’ involvement may develop over time into additional service, community and governance roles. Originality/value This paper offers practice-based insight into a flexible, episodic volunteering model within a national dementia charity. It illustrates how time-limited supported breaks and day activities can provide accessible routes into volunteering and how structured opportunities may enable volunteers to progress from direct service support into advocacy, community engagement and governance. By bringing together accounts shaped by professional training, lived experience of caring and retirement from health care, this paper shows how different motivations and life circumstances can be accommodated within one volunteer programme.

title: Value construction in live-streaming commerce: low-price tactics, diagnostic cues and continued purchase intention
journal: Asia Pacific Journal of Marketing and Logistics
abstract: Purpose Low-price live-streaming shopping (LSS) creates a psychological tension between seeking a “good deal” and product-quality concerns. This study explains how low-price tactics and heterogeneous real-time diagnostic cues shape acquisition and transaction value and how both relate to continued purchase intention. Design/methodology/approach This study draws on acquisition-transaction utility theory and the accessibility-diagnosticity model to develop a research model. Survey data from 435 repeat buyers on Facebook Live are analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). Findings Both acquisition and transaction value showed significant positive paths to continued purchase intention, with a larger estimated coefficient for transaction value. Discounts and smart-shopper feelings were both positively associated with acquisition and transaction value, with higher point estimates for smart-shopper feelings. This pattern is consistent with a self-evaluative route alongside the monetary role of price discounts. Real-time diagnostic cues showed differentiated patterns. Streamer-provided vicarious experience was positively related to both value dimensions. Positive word-of-mouth (WOM) diagnosticity showed a significant path only to transaction value, whereas negative WOM diagnosticity showed a significant path only to acquisition value. Originality/value This study frames value construction in low-price LSS as a dual-dimensional process. Within this process, the diagnostic relevance of real-time cues varies across product-worth and deal-attractiveness judgments. The study also identifies smart-shopper feelings as a self-evaluative basis of value formation alongside objective price cues.

title: Urban fascia: exploring the crossroads of urban design and hydrological heritage
abstract: Purpose Rapid urbanization and infrastructure-led transformation have fragmented the relationship between historic water systems and contemporary urban landscapes, reducing many hydrological heritage structures to isolated monuments disconnected from ecological and social functions. This paper investigates the relationship between hydrological heritage and urban design through the case of Istanbul's Kirkçesme water supply system. It aims to reinterpret the city's layered water memory by framing this Ottoman infrastructure within the contexts of sustainability, ecological resilience and cultural continuity. Design/methodology/approach The research adopts a multi-phase and multi-scalar methodology combining a literature review of 250 selected sources on historical water systems, fieldwork documenting the physical and cultural characteristics of the Kirkçesme system, spatial analysis, synthesis studies examining the identity of the study area, development of a design framework and formulation of a multi-stakeholder conservation strategy. Findings Analyses conducted in the Kemerburgaz and Göktürk areas revealed strong interactions between hydrology, land use and urban pressures, alongside flood risks and ecosystem degradation. In response, a 1:10,000 strategic master plan and a 1:1,000 urban design proposal were developed to strengthen ecological connectivity, green infrastructure continuity and the visibility of water heritage. The findings demonstrate that historic water infrastructures can function as ecological and cultural landscape systems supporting urban resilience. Research limitations/implications The chosen methodology may limit generalisability. Further testing in different contexts is recommended to validate the findings. Practical implications The proposed model informs sustainable urban planning by aligning historical water infrastructure with climate-adaptive, nature-based design. It serves as a guide for planners and local authorities. Social implications The study raises awareness of cultural water heritage and promotes inclusive, environmentally responsible planning. It supports equitable access to green-blue spaces and community identity. Originality/value The study reinterprets water heritage as an active component of ecological infrastructure and urban resilience rather than solely an object of architectural conservation. Through a multi-scalar framework, the research links heritage conservation with urban design and climate-adaptive planning strategies. Future research may expand this framework through comparative studies in other historic metropolitan contexts.

abstract: Depression is a chronic multifactorial psychiatric disorder and remains one of the leading causes of reduced quality of life. It is characterized by persistent low mood, anhedonia, and disturbances in sleep, appetite, and emotional regulation.

title: Artificial intelligence-driven transformation in healthcare: the mediating role of technostress in the impact of openness to organizational change and attitude toward AI on innovative behavior
journal: Journal of Health Organization and Management
abstract: Purpose The rapid proliferation of artificial intelligence (AI) applications in healthcare is transforming the ways in which employees interact with technology, making it crucial to understand the effects of this process on employee behavior. The purpose of this study is to examine the effects of openness to organizational change and attitudes toward AI on employees' innovative behavior, and to test the mediating role of technostress in these effects. Design/methodology/approach The research was conducted using a quantitative research design. Data were collected via face-to-face surveys from 305 healthcare workers employed at a university hospital in Istanbul, Türkiye, between January and February 2026 and analyzed using structural equation modeling. SPSS and AMOS software were used to analyze the collected data. Findings The findings revealed that employees with high levels of openness to organizational change and a positive attitude toward AI experienced lower levels of technostress, and that this, in turn, increased their innovative work behavior. Additionally, it was determined that technostress plays a partial mediating role in the effects of openness to organizational change and a positive attitude toward AI on innovative behavior. Research limitations/implications In conclusion, it has been demonstrated that employees' perceptions of technology and their openness to change shape innovative behavior through technostress in AI-driven transformation processes. Originality/value This study contributes to the literature by integrating digital transformation, organizational behavior, and health management; it also provides practical implications highlighting the importance of employee-centered digital transformation strategies for healthcare organizations and policymakers.
